titre.sous: much, many, few, little, each, every

lignes.exemple: **a lot of** emails, **a lot of** time

each.titre: each and every: singular noun, singular verb

q.lu: We did not receive ------- **information** about the delay.

etapes.texte: Look at the **noun after** the blank: plural or uncountable?

phrases.texte: Quantifiers: much, many, few and little.
The key question is: can you count the noun? Chairs, emails, employees: yes.
Time, money, information: no. These nouns have no plural.
Many, few and a few go with a plural noun: many emails, a few chairs.
phrases.dit: Many, few, and a few, go with a plural noun: many emails, a few chairs.

phrases.texte: Much, little and a little go with an uncountable noun: much time, a little money.
phrases.dit: Much, little, and a little, go with an uncountable noun: much time, a little money.

phrases.texte: A lot of and some go with both.
phrases.dit: A lot of, and some, go with both.

phrases.texte: One trap. Each and every take a singular noun and a singular verb.
phrases.dit: One trap. Each, and every, take a singular noun, and a singular verb.

phrases.texte: We say: every employee has a badge.
Now, a TOEIC question. We did not receive, blank, information about the delay.
A: many. B: much. C: few. D: every.
phrases.dit: Answer A. many. Answer B. much. Answer C. few. Answer D. every.

phrases.texte: Look at the noun after the blank: information. You cannot count it. It never takes an S.
Many and few need a plural noun. Every needs a countable noun.
phrases.dit: Many, and few, need a plural noun. Every, needs a countable noun.

phrases.texte: B is correct: we did not receive much information about the delay.
Three steps. One: look at the noun after the blank. Is it plural, or uncountable?
Two: many and few with a plural. Much and little with an uncountable noun.
Three: information, advice, equipment and furniture are never plural.
Now practise with the questions below.
phrases.dit: Now, practise with the questions below.
